course_name_original: German B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 1/3
course_name_en: German B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 1/3
prerequisites: German language knowledge at least A-2 level.

learning_outcomes.text: Can write understandable informative and argumentative texts on general and industry topics, conduct correspondence typical of the work environment, and independently use didactic materials.
Can clearly present conclusions and opinions on general, academic, and professional topics in written and oral form.
Understands longer, even complex written and oral statements, e.g., lectures and presentations, provided they concern industry issues and current affairs, and can interpret the acquired information.

Can use grammatical structures, phraseology, and vocabulary that allow for understanding general texts describing contemporary economic and social phenomena, academic and industry texts, and allow for fairly fluent and spontaneous communication in academic and professional environments.
Can prepare an oral presentation on academic and industry topics and participate in discussions quite fluently and spontaneously, also in a professional environment.

syllabus_topics: Grammar: Präteritum tense, Plusquamperfekt tense, Futur I tense, Subordinate clauses with weil, dass, obwohl, trotzdem, Temporal clauses with als, wenn, während, nachdem, seit, sobald, bis, bevor, solange, Adjective declination – Adjektivdeklination, Relative clauses - Relativsätze, Compound conjunctions: je ... desto ..., nicht ... sondern ..., nicht nur ... sondern auch, Weder .... noch, entweder .... oder, Passive voice - Passiv, Passive with modal verbs, Verb government – Verben mit Präpositionen, Subjunctive mood: Konjunktiv Präteritum und Plusquamperfekt, Irreal conditional clauses – Irreale Konditionalsätze, Conjunctions: “darum, deshalb, deswegen”, Infinitive with “zu” and without “zu” - Infinitiv mit und ohne zu, Modal particles: denn, doch, ja, eigentlich, mal, Preposition wegen, Participles: Partizip I und II, Verb “lassen”, Infinitive constructions: Infinitivkonstruktionen: um..zu, ohne…zu, anstatt…zu, Conjunctions: Konjuktionen: damit, ohne dass, anstatt dass, Adverbial clause of manner: Modalsatz indem, dadurch dass, Temporal adverbs, Negation words, Multi-part conjunctions: zwar……..aber, einerseits……… andererseits

Topics and Vocabulary: Communication media - Kommunikatiosmedien, Computer und Internet, Holidays and celebrations - Feste und Feiertage, Travel - Reisen, Housing - Wohnen, Education system in Germany and Poland - Schulen in Deutschland und in Polen, Climate and environment, weather, environmental pollution - Klima und Umwelt: Wetter, Umweltprobleme, Professional life - Berufsleben, berufliche Ziele, Cultural events - Musik, Veranstaltungen, Lifelong learning - Lebenslanges Lernen, Learning foreign languages - Fremdsprachenlernen, Job application – Bewerbug, Suche nach der Arbeit, Finance, banking, conducting business phone calls - Fit für Finanzen, Fit am Telefon, Fit für die Firma, Studies, description of the faculty and nature of studies, Industry-specific vocabulary.

Language Functions and Other Skills: Leading discussions – eine Diskussion führen, Commenting on information - Informationen kommentieren, Discussing photos and memories - Über Fotos und Erinnerungen sprechen, Discussing everyday situations - Über Alltagsprobleme sprechen, Giving advice – Ratschläge geben, Expressing wishes – Wünsche ausdrücken, Forecasting - Prognosen machen, Stating reasons -Gründe nennen, Naming conditions and consequences -Bedingungen und Konsequenzen nennen, Conflict resolution, reacting in conflict situations -Konflikte erkennen, verstehen und lösen, Discussing rules of behavior and gestures -Über Verhaltensregeln und Gesten sprechen, Conducting short conversations with randomly met people (Smalltalksituationen), Proposing and arguing, presenting one's own position, constructive criticism, Preparing and conducting a job interview, Filling out forms, Drafting various types of texts: emails and private and official letters, e.g., cover letter, CV, letters to the editor as a reaction to a read article, Listening comprehension of interviews, general conversations, and popular science statements, Reading comprehension of popular science texts, Conducting a professional presentation related to the field of study.
assessment_rules: A positive grade from all quizzes conducted during the semester is required to pass. In case of a negative grade, the student has the right to improve it; the improved grade replaces the negative one for the first retake, or the average of the two grades is taken for the second retake (the average cannot be less than 3.0). Unexcused absence from a test results in losing the term; each student is entitled to two retake quizzes. The final grade for the language course is calculated as the arithmetic mean of all grades obtained by the student from passing individual semesters and the foreign language exam. Admission to the exam requires passing the compulsory language course semesters.
